params.slug: The document's address: the part after `markdrop.in/`.
params.workspace_id: The workspace's id, from the address of its settings page (`markdrop.in/settings/workspaces/<workspace-id>`) or from [List workspaces](/api/workspaces/list-workspaces).
params.upload_id: The `upload_id` that [Start a file upload](/api/files/start-a-file-upload) returned.
params.x-edit-secret: The document's edit secret (`sk_…`), for a document published without an account. See [Edit key](/documents/edit-key).
params.x-read-password: The password of a password-protected document.
params.x-markdrop-workspace: A workspace's id: answer only if the document is in that workspace, else `404`. Workspace domains send it; you rarely need it.
params.block: The sign-off block's id (`b-…`), from [List sign-offs](/api/sign-off/list-sign-offs).

fields.title: Shown on the page and in link previews.
fields.custom_slug: Your own address: `markdrop.in/<custom_slug>`. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Taken or reserved addresses answer `409`.
fields.expires_in: When the document is deleted. `custom` needs `custom_expires_at`.
fields.custom_expires_at: The deletion time, when `expires_in` is `custom`. Must be in the future.
fields.read_password: Readers must enter this password before they see the content.
fields.access_level: Who can open it: `link` (anyone with the link), `private` (only you and the people you share it with) or `workspace` (members of its workspace).
fields.access_sync: A sign-in change (`require_auth_to_view` on or off) still applying to stored files, page images and cached pages: `state` (`applying` or `done`), `pending` and `total` items, and `want` (the setting being applied). The sign-in gate itself holds as soon as the change is saved. `null` when none was ever applied.
fields.workspace: File it in this workspace: the workspace's id.
fields.folder: An existing folder of `workspace`: its id or its path, like `guides/setup`.
fields.encrypted: Set by clients that encrypt in the browser: `content` and `title` are already ciphertext. The server never sees the key.
fields.DocumentResponse.workspace_url: The address on its workspace's own domain, when it has a live one.
fields.DocumentResponse.kind: `markdown` for a document, `artifact` for a file.
fields.DocumentResponse.can: What you may do with it: `edit`, `replace`, `settings`, `access`, `rename`, `delete`, `share`, `move`, `unshare`.
fields.DocumentCreateResponse.edit_secret: Returned once. Send it as `X-Edit-Secret` to change or delete a document published without a token.
fields.UploadCreateRequest.file_name: The file's name, with its extension.
fields.UploadCreateRequest.size_bytes: The file's exact size in bytes.
fields.UploadCreateRequest.sha256: The SHA-256 of the whole file, in hex. The server checks it before the file goes live.
fields.UploadCreateRequest.target_slug: Replace the file behind this existing address instead of publishing a new one. The link, access and views stay.
fields.UploadCompleteRequest.parts: Each part's number and the `ETag` storage returned when you uploaded it.
fields.UploadUrlsRequest.part_numbers: The parts that need a fresh URL. Leave it out for every part not yet uploaded.
fields.LevelUpdate.level: `link` (anyone with the link), `private` (only the people you share it with) or `workspace` (members of its workspace).
fields.GrantCreate.email: The person's email address. They don't need an account yet.
fields.GrantCreate.role: `viewer` can open it; `editor` can also change it.
fields.GrantCreate.notify: Notify them: an email with a link (and the message), plus a notification under the bell for people with a Markdrop account.
fields.GrantCreate.message: A note included in the email.
fields.AccessRequestDecision.decision: `view` or `edit` approves with that role; `decline` refuses.
fields.DomainCreate.kind: `app` serves documents and files; `cdn` serves files only.
fields.WorkspaceDeleteRequest.confirm_name: The workspace's name, typed back, to confirm.
fields.FolderCreate.parent_id: Create it inside this folder. Leave it out for the top level.
fields.TokenCreateRequest.name: A name to recognise it by, like the script or device that uses it.
fields.ApiTokenCreateResponse.token: The token. Shown only in this response: store it now.
fields.PreferencesUpdate.analytics_digest: `weekly` sends the weekly analytics email; `off` stops it.
fields.SlugChangeRequest.new_slug: The new address. The old one keeps working as a redirect for people who can read the document.
fields.ItemsAdd.folder_id: File them in this folder. Leave it out for the top level.
fields.ItemsAdd.access: Also change who can open them. Left out, their access doesn't change.
fields.ItemsMove.folder_id: The destination folder, or `null` for the top level.
fields.FolderShare.level: `link`: anyone with the folder link; `workspace`: members only. Each visitor still sees only the documents they could already open.
fields.PreferencesUpdate.mention_emails: `false` stops the emails about mentions and sign-off requests; `true` turns them back on. They still show under the bell.
fields.AccessRequestCreate.role: `viewer` (the default) asks to open it; `editor` asks to edit a document you can already read.
fields.PageCreate.parent: The address of a page you can edit: the new page goes inside it, in its workspace and folder, with its access. Leave `workspace` and `folder` out.
fields.PageCreate.template: A template's id, from [List every template](/api/templates/list-every-template). Leave it out for a blank page.
fields.PageCreate.slug: Your own address: `markdrop.in/<slug>`. Random when left out; `409` when taken.
fields.PageCreate.auto_cover: `false`: no cover is picked for it.
fields.PageCreateResponse.edit_secret: The new page's edit secret. Not returned on a workspace's own domain.
fields.ParentMoveRequest.parent: The address of the page to put it in, or `null` for the top level.
fields.ParentMoveRequest.confirm_access_change: Move it even though that changes who can read it.
fields.EditorSwitchRequest.editor: `blocks` for the block editor, `classic` for the Markdown editor.
fields.EmbedsRequest.slugs: Addresses of the embedded items, up to 100.
fields.TemplateSave.name: The template's name. Defaults to the page's title.
fields.TemplateSave.scope: `workspace` (the default for a page in a workspace) or `personal`.
fields.TemplateSave.workspace: Save it to this workspace instead of the page's own (members and up).
fields.TemplateSave.include_subpages: Copy the sub-pages you can open too.
fields.TemplateOrder.workspace: The workspace whose templates these are. Leave it out for your personal ones.
fields.TemplateOrder.ids: The templates' ids, in the new order.
fields.TemplateToggle.template: `true` makes the page a template; `false` makes it a page again.
fields.FolderDefaultTemplate.template: A built-in template's id, or a workspace template's id. `null`: new pages start blank.
fields.TransformBody.lang: For `translate`: the language, in English, like `Spanish`.
fields.TransformBody.before: Text just before the selection, for context.
fields.TransformBody.after: Text just after the selection, for context.
fields.WriteBody.before: Text just before the cursor, for context.
fields.WriteBody.after: Text just after the cursor, for context.
fields.NotesBody.template: A built-in template's id to shape the page, or `auto` to let AI choose.
fields.NotesBody.title: A title for the page.
fields.NotesBody.workspace: The workspace the page will go in (members and up). Its AI setting and limits apply.
fields.ActionItemsBody.text: Look only in this selection instead of the whole page.
fields.TranslateBody.lang: The language, in English: `Spanish`, `Japanese`, `Chinese (Simplified)` and so on. [Check AI availability](/api/page-ai/check-ai-availability) lists them.
fields.AltTextBody.asset_id: The image's id: the `<id>` of `asset:<id>` in the page.
fields.app__routers__pages_ai__AskBody.question: Your question.
fields.app__routers__pages_ai__AskBody.history: Earlier questions and answers in this conversation, as `{q, a}`, oldest first.
fields.SchemaPut.properties: The whole schema: up to 30 properties, each `{name, type, options?}` (`key` optional; made from the name). Types: `select`, `multi_select`, `person`, `date`, `text`, `link`, `number` and `checkbox`.
fields.SchemaPut.base_rev: The `rev` you read. If someone changed the schema since, the answer is `409` instead of overwriting it.
fields.ViewsPut.views: The saved views, `table` or `board`, up to 20.
fields.ViewsPut.base_rev: The `rev` you read. If someone changed it since, the answer is `409` instead of overwriting it.
fields.ValuesPatch.values: Values by property key. `null` clears one.
fields.ValuesPatch.base_rev: The page's `rev` you read. If it changed since, the answer is `409` instead of overwriting it.
fields.SignRequest.option: One of the block's options, or `null` to clear your decision.

GET /api/v1/home.title: Get your home
GET /api/v1/home.description: What the app's home shows, decided for you now: unread notifications and access requests waiting on you (`attention`), the open to-dos that @mention you in pages you can read (`actions`, with `can_tick` when you may edit the page), the latest meetings across your workspaces (`meetings`), your workspaces with people, item and meeting counts (`workspaces`), and whether Google Meet is connected (`meet`). No AI is used.

POST /api/v1/home/actions/tick.title: Tick one of your to-dos
POST /api/v1/home/actions/tick.description: Marks a to-do that @mentions you done (`- [ ]` becomes `- [x]`, found by its block id) through the normal save path, as you. Send `"done": false` to open it again. You need to be able to edit the page.

responses.403: You can't edit the page, or the to-do doesn't mention you.
responses.404: The page or the to-do is gone, or you can't open it.

POST /api/v1/me/previews.title: Preview items anywhere
POST /api/v1/me/previews.description: Card previews (the start of a page or document, a file's first page or cells, a thumbnail) for items in any place you can open: your own, shared with you, in any workspace. Each answers `locked` unless you can open it right now, `encrypted` for end-to-end encrypted documents and `pending` while a picture is being made.

POST /api/v1/documents.title: Publish a document
POST /api/v1/documents.description: Creates a Markdown document and returns its link. Works without an account: send a token to own it. Keep the `edit_secret` from a call without a token: it is the only way to change or delete that document later.

# Release notes

Updated from the API.

DELETE /api/v1/documents/{slug}.title: Delete a document
DELETE /api/v1/documents/{slug}.description:
Moves a document to the trash for 30 days. Its link stops working at once; [Restore from the trash](/api/trash/restore-from-the-trash) brings it back as it was. Send a token as the owner, or the document's edit secret in `X-Edit-Secret`.

A page with sub-pages needs `children`: `delete` sends them to the trash with it, `lift` moves them up a level.

paramNotes.children: For a page with sub-pages: `delete` (they go to the trash too) or `lift` (they move up a level).

responses.409: The page has sub-pages and `children` is missing: `code` is `has_children`, with their `count`.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/edit-secre.title: Rotate the edit secret
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/edit-secre.description: Replaces a document's edit secret, for when the old one leaked. The old secret stops working at once; the new one is in the response, once. Owner only.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/claim.title: Claim a document
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/claim.description: Adds a document you published without an account to your account. Send its edit secret in `X-Edit-Secret`.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/copy.title: Copy a document
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/copy.description: Makes a copy of a document you can read, owned by you, with a new address, no password and no expiry. The copy is private unless the original is open to anyone with the link.

PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/slug.title: Change the address
PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/slug.description: Gives a document a new address. Its old address keeps working for people who can read it.

responses.409: That address is taken, or reserved.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/slug-check.title: Check an address
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/slug-check.description: Whether a document could move to `new_slug`, without changing anything: `available`, or a `code` that says why not (`same`, `invalid`, `reserved`, `taken` or `folder`), plus the links it would have on markdrop.in and on its workspace's domain. For people who may change its address.

PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/settings.title: Set password and expiry
PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/settings.description: Changes a document's password or expiry without sending its content. Every field is optional: leave one out to keep it. `"read_password": ""` removes the password. Send a token as the owner, or the edit secret.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/report.title: Report a document
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/report.description: Flags a document for abuse. Always answers `202`, whether or not the address exists.

GET /api/v1/me/documents.title: List your documents
GET /api/v1/me/documents.description: The documents and files you own, a page at a time, with counts of each kind.

paramNotes.q: Only titles or addresses containing this text.
paramNotes.per_page: Same as `limit`, up to 50; wins when both are sent.

GET /api/v1/og/{slug}.png.title: Get the preview image
GET /api/v1/og/{slug}.png.description: The 1200×630 image link previews show for a document, as PNG.

paramNotes.host: Draw the card for this address (a workspace's own domain) instead of markdrop.in.

POST /api/v1/pages.title: Create a page
POST /api/v1/pages.description: Creates a page: a document that opens in the block editor. `template` fills it from a template, or `content` gives its Markdown. `workspace` and `folder` file it (members and up); `parent` puts it inside a page you can edit, with that page's workspace, folder and access. Unless it has a cover, or `auto_cover` is `false`, a cover is picked for it in the background.

responses.201: Created. Returns the page as `document`, with its `slug` and `url`.
responses.409: `slug` is taken, or reserved. Nothing is created.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/children.title: List sub-pages
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/children.description: The pages inside a page that you can open, oldest first, each saying whether it has sub-pages of its own.

PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/parent.title: Move a page
PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/parent.description: Puts a page inside another page (`parent`: its address) or at the top level (`null`). If that changes who can read it, the answer is `409` with `code: "access_change"` and the readers before and after; send `confirm_access_change: true` to move it anyway.

responses.409: The move changes who can read the page. Send `confirm_access_change: true` to go ahead.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/backlinks.title: List backlinks
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/backlinks.description: Pages that mention, embed or link to this one, among those you can open.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/mentionable.title: List people to mention
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/mentionable.description: Who you can @-mention on a page you can edit: the members of its workspace, sorted by name, with their email address when you're a signed-in member on markdrop.in (never on a workspace's own domain). `state` is `ok`, or says why no one is listed: `personal` (the page is in no workspace), `signin` (an edit link with no account) or `not_member` (you edit it but aren't in its workspace). Write a mention as `:person[Name]{id="<id>"}`.

PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/editor.title: Switch the editor
PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/editor.description: Opens a document in the block editor (`blocks`) or the classic Markdown editor (`classic`). The Markdown doesn't change. Not for files or end-to-end encrypted documents.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock.title: Take the edit lock
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock.description: Takes, renews or takes over a page's edit lock, so nobody else edits it at the same time. Take it with your first real change (`intent=edit`) and renew it every 30 seconds while you edit (`intent=heartbeat`, with `edited`, `hidden` and `dirty`). It lapses 2 minutes after your last heartbeat, 2 minutes after your last change, or 60 seconds after your tab was hidden, whichever comes first. A heartbeat never takes back a lock that lapsed or was taken over: it answers `mine: false`, `released: true` and the `reason`. `take_over=true` lets the page's owner or a workspace admin take it from whoever holds it.

paramNotes.intent: `edit` (your first change: take it) or `heartbeat` (renew yours). Leave it out only in old clients.
paramNotes.edited: You changed something since the last heartbeat.
paramNotes.dirty: You have changes the server doesn't have yet.
paramNotes.take_over: Take it from whoever holds it. The page's owner and workspace admins only.

responses.423: Someone else is editing: `code` is `locked`, with the `holder`'s name, `idle_s`, `dirty` (unsaved changes), `releases_in_s` and `can_take_over`.
responses.403: `take_over_forbidden`: only the page's owner or a workspace admin can take over.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock.title: Check the edit lock
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock.description: Who holds a page's edit lock, without taking it: `holder` is `null` when it's free. Otherwise it says how long they've been idle, whether they have unsaved changes, when it releases by itself and whether you may take over.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock/keep.title: Keep unsaved text
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock/keep.description: Keeps text you couldn't save, because someone took over the page, as a version in its history. The page itself doesn't change.

example.content:
# Launch plan

What I was writing…

DELETE /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock.title: Release the edit lock
DELETE /api/v1/documents/{slug}/lock.description: Lets go of a page's edit lock that you hold, so others can edit it straight away.

GET /api/v1/pages/{slug}/cover.title: Get the cover
GET /api/v1/pages/{slug}/cover.description: A page's cover now, and whether an automatic cover is still being picked (`cover_pending`). For anyone who can read the page.

POST /api/v1/pages/{slug}/cover/suggest.title: Suggest a cover
POST /api/v1/pages/{slug}/cover/suggest.description: Picks a cover from the built-in gallery for what the page is about, the way new pages get one, without saving it: `cover` is `gallery:<id>`. For people who can edit the page.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/assets.title: Upload a page image
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/assets.description: Uploads a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image of up to 10 MB to a page, as `multipart/form-data`. Use the `id` it returns in the page as `![alt](asset:<id>)`. The image shows to exactly the page's readers.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/assets/urls.title: Get image links
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/assets/urls.description: Fresh links for the images a page uses, by image id, each with when it expires.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/embeds.title: Resolve embedded items
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/embeds.description: What you may see of each Markdrop item embedded in a page you can read. Each item is checked with its own access: one you can't open comes back without its title, excerpt or link.

POST /api/v1/bookmarks/preview.title: Preview a bookmark
POST /api/v1/bookmarks/preview.description: Fetches a link's title, description, site name, icon and image, for a bookmark block. The limits count per account, not per IP address.

responses.422: That address may not be fetched: a private network, another scheme or port, or credentials in the URL.

POST /api/v1/link-preview.title: Preview a link
POST /api/v1/link-preview.description: The same as [Preview a bookmark](/api/pages/preview-a-bookmark), with limits of its own.

GET /api/v1/web-embeds/providers.title: List embed providers
GET /api/v1/web-embeds/providers.description: The sites a page can embed directly, such as YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Figma, Google Maps and CodePen, each with an example link.

GET /api/v1/web-embeds/resolve.title: Resolve an embed link
GET /api/v1/web-embeds/resolve.description: The embeddable address and aspect ratio for a link from a supported site. Worked out from the link alone: nothing is fetched.

responses.422: Not a link from a supported site.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/export.title: Export a page
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/export.description: Downloads a page as portable Markdown (`md`), one self-contained HTML file (`html`), or a `.zip` with its images (`zip`). With `subpages=true` its sub-pages come too, in a `.zip`. Editors can always export; readers can unless the page turns exporting off.

responses.413: Too many pages to export at once.
responses.422: The document is end-to-end encrypted: export it from the page in your browser.

GET /api/v1/page-templates.title: List built-in templates
GET /api/v1/page-templates.description: The built-in page templates, each with its id, name, description, icon, category and Markdown.

GET /api/v1/page-templates/all.title: List every template
GET /api/v1/page-templates/all.description: Every template you can start a page from: the built-ins, your personal templates and, with `workspace`, that workspace's templates (members and up). With `folder` too, the folder's default template.

paramNotes.folder: A folder of `workspace`: its id or path.

GET /api/v1/page-templates/{template_id}.title: Get a template
GET /api/v1/page-templates/{template_id}.description: One workspace or personal template, with its Markdown and image links.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/save-as-te.title: Save as a template
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/save-as-te.description: Saves a copy of a page, with its images, as a template: the workspace's (members and up) or your own (`scope: "personal"`). `include_subpages` copies the sub-pages you can open too.

PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/template.title: Make a page a template
PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/template.description: `true` turns the page itself into a template, sub-pages included: it leaves every list and search and shows when people make a new page. `false` turns it back into a page. Pages already made from it never change.

PATCH /api/v1/page-templates/{template_i.title: Update a template
PATCH /api/v1/page-templates/{template_i.description: Renames a template, or changes its description or icon (an empty `icon` clears it). A workspace template: its admins and whoever saved it.

PUT /api/v1/page-templates/order.title: Reorder templates
PUT /api/v1/page-templates/order.description: Sets the order of a workspace's templates (admins) or, with `workspace` left out, of your personal ones.

DELETE /api/v1/page-templates/{template_.title: Delete a template
DELETE /api/v1/page-templates/{template_.description: Deletes a template and its sub-pages. Pages made from it don't change.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Set a folder's default template
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: The template new pages in a folder start from: a built-in template's id or a workspace template's id, or `null` for a blank page. Admins only. People can still choose another template.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/versions.title: List page versions
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/versions.description: A page's saved versions, newest first, with who made each one and when. For people who can edit the page. An end-to-end encrypted document has no history: `available` is `false`.

paramNotes.limit: How many to return, up to 100.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/versions/{n.title: Get a page version
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/versions/{n.description: One version's Markdown and image links, with the page as it is now (`current_doc`) to compare.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/versions/{.title: Restore a page version
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/versions/{.description: Makes version `n` the page again, as a new version. The page as it was is saved first, so a restore can be undone.

responses.423: Someone else has the page open in the editor.

GET /api/v1/ai/pages/status.title: Check AI availability
GET /api/v1/ai/pages/status.description: Which AI features you can use, on a page (`slug`) or for a new page in a workspace (`workspace`). When they're off, `enabled` is `false` and `reason` says why: `signin`, `encrypted`, `off`, `not_configured`, `workspace_off`, `blocked`, `daily` or `monthly`. It also lists the actions, tones and languages the other endpoints take.

paramNotes.workspace: A workspace's id, for a new page there.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/notes.title: Draft a page from notes
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/notes.description: Turns rough notes into a page in Markdown. Streams the result as server-sent events: `delta` events with text as it's written, then `done` (or `limit` when a limit stops it). Nothing is saved: create the page with [Create a page](/api/pages/create-a-page).

example.notes: kickoff thurs, sam owns api, ship by 20th

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/transform.title: Rewrite a selection
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/transform.description: Rewrites text from a page you can edit: improves, shortens or fixes it, changes its tone, translates it, or turns it into a checklist, a table or an explanation. Streams the result as server-sent events: `delta` events with text as it's written, then `done` (or `limit` when a limit stops it). Nothing changes on the page: the result is a suggestion.

example.text: We are going to be shipping the new release at some point next week.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/write.title: Write with a prompt
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/write.description: Writes new Markdown for a page you can edit, from `prompt` and the text around the cursor. Streams the result as server-sent events: `delta` events with text as it's written, then `done` (or `limit` when a limit stops it). Nothing changes on the page: the result is a suggestion.

example.prompt: A short FAQ about the new pricing

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/action-item.title: Find action items
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/action-item.description: Finds the action items in a page you can edit (or in `text`) and writes them as a checklist, naming workspace members where it can. Streams the result as server-sent events: `delta` events with text as it's written, then `done` (or `limit` when a limit stops it). Nothing changes on the page: the result is a suggestion.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/summary.title: Summarize a page
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/summary.description: Writes a short summary of a page you can edit, as a note titled Summary. Streams the result as server-sent events: `delta` events with text as it's written, then `done` (or `limit` when a limit stops it). Nothing changes on the page: the result is a suggestion.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/meta.title: Suggest a title and icon
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/meta.description: Suggests a title, a one-sentence description and an emoji icon for a page you can edit. Nothing is saved.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/translate.title: Translate a page
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/translate.description: Translates a page you can edit into `lang` as a new page next to it, titled with the language's name, with the same blocks, embeds and properties. The original doesn't change. Returns the new page's `slug`, `url` and `title`; send `Accept: text/event-stream` to get `progress` events while it works.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/alt-text.title: Suggest alt text
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/alt-text.description: Suggests alt text for one of the images in a page you can edit. Nothing is saved.

POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/ask.title: Ask about a page
POST /api/v1/ai/pages/{slug}/ask.description: Answers a question about a page you can read, from its content and the embedded items you can open. Send earlier turns in `history` to follow up. Streams the answer as server-sent events: `delta` events, then `done`.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Get a folder's database
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: A folder as a database: its properties, saved views and rows. The rows are the pages filed directly in the folder that you can read, newest first, up to 500. Any member.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Set a folder's properties
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: Replaces a folder's properties, and optionally its views. Members and admins. Pages' values never change: a property you leave out keeps its values, hidden.

responses.409: Someone changed the properties since your `base_rev`.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Set a folder's views
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: Replaces a folder's saved views: tables and boards, up to 20. Members and admins.

responses.409: Someone changed the views since your `base_rev`.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/properties.title: Get a page's property values
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/properties.description: A page's properties and their values, as you see them: people's names and linked pages' titles only where you may see them. `null` when its folder has no properties.

PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/propertie.title: Set a page's property values
PATCH /api/v1/documents/{slug}/propertie.description: Sets some of a page's property values, by key. `null` clears one. For people who can edit the page.

responses.422: A value doesn't fit its property, or it isn't a page.
responses.423: Someone else is editing the page, or it's locked.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/signoffs.title: List sign-offs
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/signoffs.description: The sign-off blocks on a page you can read: each one's options, the decision and who made it, and whether you can sign it. Names show only to people inside the page's circle.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/signoffs/{.title: Sign off
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/signoffs/{.description: Records your decision on a sign-off block that names you: `option` is one of its options, or `null` to clear it. Returns the block as you see it.

responses.404: No such block on the page.
responses.422: The block doesn't offer that option.

POST /api/v1/files/uploads.title: Start a file upload
POST /api/v1/files/uploads.description:
Starts publishing a file of any size: send its name, size and SHA-256, and get back presigned URLs to `PUT` each part to. Then [finish the upload](/api/files/finish-a-file-upload). With `target_slug`, the file replaces the one behind an existing link instead, keeping the link, its access and its views.

The CLI does all of this, with resume, in one command.

responses.409: The address you asked for is taken, or reserved.
responses.413: The file is over the size limit for its type.

POST /api/v1/files/uploads/{upload_id}/u.title: Get fresh part URLs
POST /api/v1/files/uploads/{upload_id}/u.description: New presigned URLs for parts of an upload in progress, for when the first ones expired before you used them.

GET /api/v1/files/uploads/{upload_id}.title: Check an upload
GET /api/v1/files/uploads/{upload_id}.description: Where an upload stands: how many parts arrived and, once finished, whether the check passed (`state` is `done`, with `result`) or failed (`failed`, with `error`).

POST /api/v1/files/uploads/{upload_id}/c.title: Finish a file upload
POST /api/v1/files/uploads/{upload_id}/c.description: Publishes the file once every part is uploaded. The server checks the SHA-256 first. `200` returns the link. `202` (`{"state": "verifying"}`) means the check is still running: [check the upload](/api/files/check-an-upload) until `state` is `done`. Calling it again on a finished upload returns the same result.

responses.202: Still checking the file. Poll the upload's status.

GET /api/v1/files/{slug}.title: Get file details
GET /api/v1/files/{slug}.description: A published file's size, type, current version, SHA-256 and, for video and audio, its duration and dimensions.

GET /api/v1/files/{slug}/versions.title: List file versions
GET /api/v1/files/{slug}/versions.description: Every version of a file you own or can edit. Replacing a file keeps the previous version.

POST /api/v1/files/{slug}/versions/{vers.title: Restore a file version
POST /api/v1/files/{slug}/versions/{vers.description: Makes an earlier version current again, at the same link. Versions start at 1.

DELETE /api/v1/files/{slug}/versions/{ve.title: Delete a file version
DELETE /api/v1/files/{slug}/versions/{ve.description: Deletes one earlier version for good and frees its space. Only the file's owner can do this, and never for the current version.

responses.403: You can edit the file but don't own it.
responses.409: That's the current version. Restore another one first, or delete the file.

POST /api/v1/artifacts/paste.title: Publish an HTML page
POST /api/v1/artifacts/paste.description: Publishes HTML you send in the request as a page that renders. Up to 10 MB; anything larger goes through [Start a file upload](/api/files/start-a-file-upload).

POST /api/v1/artifacts/upload-url.title: Get a single upload URL
POST /api/v1/artifacts/upload-url.description: The one-request upload markdrop.in uses for smaller files: returns a presigned URL to `PUT` the whole file to, then [publish it](/api/files/publish-an-uploaded-file). For anything large, or to resume, use [Start a file upload](/api/files/start-a-file-upload).

responses.413: The file is over the size limit for its type.

POST /api/v1/artifacts.title: Publish an uploaded file
POST /api/v1/artifacts.description: Publishes a file uploaded with [Get a single upload URL](/api/files/get-a-single-upload-url), after checking its real size and type.

PATCH /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}.title: Update a file's settings
PATCH /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}.description: Changes a file's title, password or expiry. Every field is optional. The owner may change all of them; editors may change the title.

PUT /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}/file.title: Replace a file
PUT /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}/file.description: Swaps the file behind a link for one uploaded with [Get a single upload URL](/api/files/get-a-single-upload-url), keeping the link and its settings. The previous file is kept as a version.

PUT /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}/captions.title: Add captions to a video
PUT /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}/captions.description: Adds or replaces a video's captions from a WebVTT (.vtt) or SubRip (.srt) file's text, at most 2 MB. The player shows them as subtitles, and search and Ask read the video by minute. Needs edit rights on the file.

responses.422: Not a video, or no captions found in the text (use a .vtt or .srt file).

DELETE /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}/captions.title: Remove a video's captions
DELETE /api/v1/artifacts/{slug}/captions.description: Removes a video's captions: the player stops showing them and search and Ask stop reading them.

GET /api/v1/trash.title: List the trash
GET /api/v1/trash.description: What you can restore: your own deleted documents, pages, files and folders, and everything deleted from workspaces you administer. Newest first; a folder deleted with its contents is one row. Items stay 30 days.

paramNotes.workspace: Only what was deleted from this workspace (its id).

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/delete-prev.title: Preview a delete
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/delete-prev.description: What deleting a document would take, before you do it: its kind, title and link, and how many sub-pages sit below it (`children` directly, `descendants` in all). For people who may delete it.

POST /api/v1/trash/{slug}/restore.title: Restore from the trash
POST /api/v1/trash/{slug}/restore.description: Puts a deleted item back where it was, with the same link, access and people, together with what was deleted with it: a page's sub-pages, or a folder's folders and items. If the place it came from is gone, it comes back as close as it can and `notes` says where. Send a token as its owner or an admin of its workspace, or the document's edit secret.

paramNotes.slug: The item's address, or a deleted folder's id, from [List the trash](/api/trash/list-the-trash).

DELETE /api/v1/trash/{slug}.title: Delete forever
DELETE /api/v1/trash/{slug}.description: Deletes an item in the trash, and what was deleted with it, for good. This can't be undone. `items` lists what was deleted.

paramNotes.slug: The item's address, or a deleted folder's id, from [List the trash](/api/trash/list-the-trash).

GET /api/v1/trash/lookup/{slug}.title: Look up a deleted item
GET /api/v1/trash/lookup/{slug}.description: What a link to a deleted item says to someone who could edit it: what it was, who deleted it and when, when it's deleted for good, and whether you can restore it. Anyone else gets `404`, the same as an address that doesn't exist.

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access.title: Get sharing settings
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access.description: Who can open a document and the people it is shared with. People with a role on the document can call it; the list of people is for the owner and editors.

PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/leve.title: Set who can open it
PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/leve.description: Sets a document's access level. Narrowing it takes effect at once, for every address the document has.

POST /api/v1/documents/access/level.title: Set access for several documents
POST /api/v1/documents/access/level.description: Sets the access level of many documents you own at once. Each one is checked on its own: the response has a result per address.

PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/resh.title: Let editors share
PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/resh.description: Whether editors may share the document with more people.

PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/pres.title: Show who's viewing
PUT /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/pres.description: Turns the document's **Show who's viewing** on or off. Owner only. Off, nobody on the page sees anyone, not even a count.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/peo.title: Share with a person
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access/peo.description: Gives one person access by email, and optionally emails them. If the email fails, the access stays: the response says whether it was sent.

POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access-req.title: Request access
POST /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access-req.description: Asks the owner of a document you can't open for access, or, with `role: "editor"`, for edit access to one you can read. The owner can approve or decline it.

example.message: Could I see the Q3 numbers?

GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access-requ.title: Check your request
GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/access-requ.description: Whether your request for access to a document is pending, approved or declined.

paramNotes.role: `editor` checks your request for edit access instead.

GET /api/v1/me/access-requests.title: List requests for you
GET /api/v1/me/access-requests.description: Requests for access to documents you own.

GET /api/v1/access-requests/{request_id}.title: Get an access request
GET /api/v1/access-requests/{request_id}.description: One request for access to a document you own.

POST /api/v1/access-requests/{request_id.title: Answer an access request
POST /api/v1/access-requests/{request_id.description: Approves a request as a viewer or editor, or declines it.

GET /api/v1/notifications.title: List notifications
GET /api/v1/notifications.description: Your notifications from the last 90 days, newest first: someone mentioned you, asked for your sign-off or shared a page with you. One about a page you can no longer open has no title or link.

paramNotes.limit: How many to return, up to 100.

GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count.title: Count unread notifications
GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count.description: How many of your notifications are unread. The bell calls this while Markdrop is open in a visible tab, so it also counts as having seen what came before (no email about it).

paramNotes.tz: Your IANA time zone, such as `Europe/Berlin`. The daily email digest goes at 8:00 there.

POST /api/v1/notifications/read.title: Mark notifications read
POST /api/v1/notifications/read.description: Marks some notifications read (`ids`), or all of them (`all: true`). Returns how many changed and the new unread count.

POST /api/v1/notifications/{notification.title: Open a notification
POST /api/v1/notifications/{notification.description: Marks a notification read and returns the link to the page and block it's about, if you can open that page now.

responses.403: You can't open the page now, or it's gone.

GET /api/v1/workspaces.title: List workspaces
GET /api/v1/workspaces.description: The workspaces you belong to, with your role in each and their live domains.

POST /api/v1/workspaces.title: Create a workspace
POST /api/v1/workspaces.description: Creates a workspace with you as its owner.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Get a workspace
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: A workspace's name, branding, settings and your role in it.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Update a workspace
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: Changes a workspace's name, branding or settings. Every field is optional. Turning `require_auth_to_view` on or off takes effect for readers at once; files, page images and cached pages follow in the background, and the answer's `access_sync` says how many items are still applying (`GET` the workspace to follow it).

DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Delete a workspace
DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: Deletes a workspace, its folders and its domains. Documents filed in it are not deleted: they go back to their owners. Send the workspace's name to confirm.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/me.title: List members
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/me.description: Everyone in a workspace, with their roles.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/me.title: Change a member's role
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/me.description: Makes a member an admin, a member or a viewer.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/me.title: Find members to mention
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/me.description: Up to 20 members of a workspace whose name or email contains `q`, for mentioning in a page: their id, name and picture, never their email. Any member can search.

paramNotes.q: Part of a name or email. Leave it empty for everyone.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/in.title: List invitations
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/in.description: Invitations that haven't been answered yet.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.title: Invite someone
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.description: Emails someone an invitation to join the workspace.

DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Revoke an invitation
DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: Withdraws an invitation that hasn't been answered yet.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/b.title: Upload a logo or favicon
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/b.description: Uploads an image and returns its URL. It isn't used until you save that URL in the workspace's branding with [Update a workspace](/api/workspaces/update-a-workspace).

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/t.title: Transfer ownership
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/t.description: Makes another member the owner. You become an admin. Documents, sharing and domains don't change. Owner only.

GET /api/v1/og/w/{workspace_id}.png.title: Get a workspace's preview image
GET /api/v1/og/w/{workspace_id}.png.description: The 1200×630 image link previews show for a workspace's address, as PNG. It names the workspace only when a signed-out visitor could see it: it has a live domain and doesn't require sign-in. Otherwise the card is blank.

GET /api/v1/invites/{token}.title: Preview an invitation
GET /api/v1/invites/{token}.description: What an invitation link is for: the workspace, the role and whether it is still open. Answers `200` for invitations already accepted or withdrawn too, saying so.

paramNotes.token: The token from the invitation link.

POST /api/v1/invites/{token}/accept.title: Accept an invitation
POST /api/v1/invites/{token}/accept.description: Joins the workspace with the role the invitation offers, as the account the token belongs to.

paramNotes.token: The token from the invitation link.

POST /api/v1/invites/{token}/decline.title: Decline an invitation
POST /api/v1/invites/{token}/decline.description: Turns an invitation down. No token needed: the invitation link is enough.

paramNotes.token: The token from the invitation link.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/f.title: Create a folder
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/f.description: Creates a folder at the top level, or inside another folder with `parent_id`. If a folder, page, document or file there already has the folder's address, it returns `409` saying what holds it and creates nothing (an item you can't open is never named and never blocks you: the folder takes the next free address); send `on_conflict: "suffix"` to take the next free address (`guides-2`) instead.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Update a folder
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: Renames a folder, or moves it with `parent_id` and `reparent: true`. A new address that is already taken there is a `409` unless you send `on_conflict: "suffix"`. The folder's old address redirects to the new one.

PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/.title: Rename or move a folder
PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/.description: Renames a folder, changes its address, moves it (`parent_id`; `null` is the top level) or sets the access new documents in it start with. Admins and the owner. Every document below it moves to its new address, and the old addresses (the folder's own included) redirect. A new address that is already taken there is a `409` unless you send `on_conflict: "suffix"`.

DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Delete a folder
DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: Deletes a folder. By default (`mode=trash`) the folder, every folder inside it and everything filed in them go to the trash for 30 days, and come back together if you restore the folder. With `unfile` or `move_up` only the folder goes: what was in it moves to the top of the workspace, or into the parent folder.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/tr.title: Get the folder tree
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/tr.description: The workspace's folders as a tree, with their paths.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/it.title: List workspace items
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/it.description: The documents and folders in a workspace that you can see.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/na.title: Get the sidebar outline
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/na.description: A compact outline of a workspace for a sidebar: the top-level items you can read, grouped by folder, up to 50 a folder. `more` counts the rest per folder. Any member.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/pr.title: Preview as someone else
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/pr.description: What another person would see in a folder, and what is hidden from them and why. Members can preview; previewing a named person (`as` set to an email) is for admins.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.title: File documents
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.description: Files documents you own into the workspace. Their access stays the same unless you send `access`.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.title: Preview items
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.description: What the Cards view shows of each item, for up to 12 items at a time. Each answers `locked` unless you can open it right now, `encrypted` for an end-to-end encrypted document, and `pending` while a picture is being made (ask again). Otherwise `ok` with plain-text `blocks` (pages, documents, HTML and Word files), a sheet's first `rows`, a text file's first `lines`, or `src`, a small WebP thumbnail as a data URI (images, a PDF's first page, a video's poster, a page's cover). An HTML file also has `live`, its signed address on the files origin. Any member.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.title: Move documents
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.description: Moves documents to another folder. Every document is checked first: if you can't move one, none move.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.title: Take documents out
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/i.description: Takes documents out of the workspace. They go back to their owners. A document with `workspace` access becomes `private`.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.title: Move a document
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.description: Moves one document to a folder (`folder_id`), or to the top level (`null`).

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Share a folder
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: Creates a link to a folder. Each visitor sees only the documents they could already open: sharing a folder never changes any document's access. `hidden` lists what the link's audience can't see.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.title: Get a folder's link
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/fo.description: The folder's share, or `404` when it isn't shared.

GET /api/v1/folders/shared/{share_id}.title: Open a shared folder
GET /api/v1/folders/shared/{share_id}.description: What a shared folder link shows: the folder, its subfolders and the documents in it that you can open. A folder shared with `workspace` access needs a member's token.

GET /api/v1/og/w/{workspace_id}/f/{folde.title: Get a folder's preview image
GET /api/v1/og/w/{workspace_id}/f/{folde.description: The 1200×630 image link previews show for a folder's address, as PNG. It names the folder only when a signed-out visitor could already see it: the folder is shared with anyone with the link, or it holds items anyone can open on a workspace with a live domain. Otherwise the card is blank.

GET /api/v1/og/f/{share_id}.png.title: Get a shared folder's preview image
GET /api/v1/og/f/{share_id}.png.description: The image link previews show for a shared folder's link (`markdrop.in/f/<share-id>`), as PNG, with the same rules as [Get a folder's preview image](/api/folders/get-a-folder-s-preview-image).

paramNotes.path: A subfolder's path below the shared folder.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.title: List workspace documents
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.description: The documents filed in a workspace.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.title: Add a document
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.description: Files one of your documents in the workspace, by its id.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.title: Count workspace documents
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.description: How many documents a workspace has in each folder.

DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Remove a document
DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: Takes a document out of the workspace. It isn't deleted: it goes back to its owner unchanged.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.title: File in a folder
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.description: Puts a workspace document in a folder, or at the top level with `null`.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.title: List domains
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.description: A workspace's custom domains and where each one stands.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.title: Add a domain
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.description: Adds a domain to a workspace and returns the DNS records to create at your DNS provider.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.title: Verify a domain
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.description: Checks the domain's DNS records now, instead of waiting for the next automatic check.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.title: Turn on a domain
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.description: Starts serving a verified domain, with HTTPS.

responses.501: Domains can't be turned on automatically here. Finish the step by hand.

POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.title: Take a domain offline
POST /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/d.description: Stops serving a domain without losing its verification, so you can turn it back on later.

GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.title: Detect the DNS provider
GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.description: Which DNS provider the domain uses, so setup instructions can name the right screens. Makes a live DNS lookup.

PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.title: Set the primary domain
PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/do.description: Chooses the domain the workspace's links and previews use. Admins and the owner.

DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.title: Remove a domain
DELETE /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}.description: Removes a domain from the workspace. Links on it stop working; the documents keep their markdrop.in addresses.

GET /api/v1/me/analytics.title: Analytics for everything
GET /api/v1/me/analytics.description: Totals across every document and file you own.

GET /api/v1/me/analytics/live.title: Who is reading now
GET /api/v1/me/analytics/live.description: People reading or watching your documents right now.

GET /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/status.title: Check Analytics AI availability
GET /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/status.description: Whether Insights, Ask and Write this next can run now. When they can't, `enabled` is `false`, `reason` says why (`off`, `not_configured`, `blocked`, `burst`, `user_daily`, `daily` or `monthly`) and `message` says it in words. `gap_scopes` lists where you may see content gaps: each workspace you own or admin (`workspace:<id>`) and `personal` when you have Guides of your own.

GET /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/story.title: What changed (AI)
GET /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/story.description: Insights for the analytics home: a `headline` and 3 to 5 `bullets`, each a sentence on what changed against the period before and the likely cause, with an `href` to the analytics page to look at (and `doc` when it's about one of your links). AI writes it from totals and your own titles only. Kept for the day (`cached: true`); `fresh=1` writes it again. `status` is `thin` when there are fewer than 20 views to go on, `limit` when an AI limit stops it (with `reason` and `message`), or `error`. Counts towards your AI limits.

paramNotes.fresh: `1` writes it again instead of using today's copy.

POST /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/ask.title: Ask your analytics (AI)
POST /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/ask.description: Answers a question about your own analytics with AI, which picks from a fixed set of queries that Markdrop runs on the documents you own (totals, top links, a link's numbers, referrers, channels, devices, countries, views by day, period comparisons, file versions). Streams server-sent events: `status` (what it's checking), `delta` (answer text; `reset: true` clears what was shown), then `done` with `answer` and `links` (only analytics pages the queries returned); or `limit`, or `error`. The same question the same day is answered from the copy kept (`cached: true`) unless `fresh` is `true`. Counts towards your AI limits.

example.question: Which link did best this month?

GET /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/gaps.title: What people couldn't find (AI)
GET /api/v1/me/analytics/ai/gaps.description: Content gaps for a workspace you own or admin (`scope=workspace:<id>`, else `403`) or your own Guides (`scope=personal`): searches that found nothing or that nobody opened, and guide questions Ask AI couldn't answer, over the last 30 days, grouped by AI into up to 5 `gaps`. Each has `topic`, `count` (counted by Markdrop), `why`, `outline`, `examples` and `markdown` ready to create a page in `create.workspace`. `status` is `thin` under 5 searches and questions. Counts towards your AI limits.

paramNotes.fresh: `1` groups them again instead of using today's copy.

GET /api/v1/me/analytics.csv.title: Export all analytics
GET /api/v1/me/analytics.csv.description: Your analytics across every document, as CSV.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Document view totals
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: View counts, unique readers, read depth and top referrers for a document. Owner only: anyone else who can read it gets `403`.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Document overview
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: The headline numbers for one document or file you own.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Video and audio retention
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: How many people are still watching or listening through a video or audio file.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Video frame
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: A frame of your video at `t` seconds, as JPEG. `404` when the file isn't a video.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Reading depth
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: How far readers get through a Markdown document, section by section.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: PDF pages reached
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: How many readers reach each page of a PDF.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Audience
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: Who a document's readers are: new or returning, their devices and countries.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Numbers by version
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: A file's numbers split by the version people saw.

GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.title: Get AI insights
GET /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytic.description: The saved AI analysis of one of your documents or files, never a new one. `kind` is `content` (documents and pages), `media` (video and audio), `pages` (PDFs) or `versions` (files with several versions). `state` is `ready` (with `result`: `summary` and 3 to 5 `findings`), `empty` (nothing yet: `POST` to analyse), `thin` (fewer than 20 sessions with data: `sample` says how many), `encrypted` or `unsupported`. `stale` is `true` when the document changed since; `limit` says why AI can't run right now.

POST /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analyti.title: Analyse with AI
POST /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analyti.description: AI reads the numbers (and your own content) and returns 3 to 5 findings that point at a section, timestamp, page or version, with rewrites (`content`), chapters (`media`) and a verdict with a confidence Markdrop computes (`versions`). Returns the saved analysis when there is one; send `{"refresh": true}` to analyse again. Below 20 sessions the model isn't called (`state: thin`). Counts towards your AI limits: `429` with `code: limit` and a `reason` when one is reached.

PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences.title: Set email preferences
PATCH /api/v1/me/preferences.description: Sets the weekly analytics email (`analytics_digest`) and how often you're emailed about mentions and sign-off requests (`email_notify`: `mention` and `signoff_requested`, each `instant`, `hourly`, `daily` or `off`). `tz` is your IANA time zone for the daily digest. `mention_emails: false` still turns both kinds off, and `true` brings back the defaults. Send any of them; the response has all of them.

GET /api/v1/auth/me.title: Get your account
GET /api/v1/auth/me.description: The account a token belongs to: id, email, name and sign-in methods. A quick way to check a token works.

GET /api/v1/me/tokens.title: List API tokens
GET /api/v1/me/tokens.description: Your API tokens: name, first characters, when each was created and last used. Never the tokens themselves.

POST /api/v1/me/tokens.title: Create an API token
POST /api/v1/me/tokens.description: Creates an API token (`mdk_…`). It is shown only in this response.

DELETE /api/v1/me/tokens/{token_id}.title: Revoke an API token
DELETE /api/v1/me/tokens/{token_id}.description: Revokes a token at once. Requests with it get `401` from then on.

GET /api/v1/me/contacts.title: Suggest people
GET /api/v1/me/contacts.description: Up to 50 people you can share with: people you shared documents with before, and members of your workspaces. Never a search of every account.

paramNotes.q: Only people whose email or name contains this text.

GET /api/v1/me/shared.title: Shared with you
GET /api/v1/me/shared.description: Documents other people shared with you, a page at a time.

GET /api/v1/search.title: Search everything
GET /api/v1/search.description: Fuzzy search over everything you can open: titles, headings, the text of pages and documents, the text of HTML files and PDFs, folders, workspaces, the Guides pages you have a role on and, at the end, your Trash. Typos, partial words and any word order match. `items` is the ranked page of results; `groups` holds the first few of each kind, for a grouped list; `trash` lists matching items you can restore. Each result has its `kind`, `title`, `workspace`, `folder`, `owner` (named only when you're related to the item), `updated_at`, a `snippet` with the matched words' ranges in `marks`, `match` (`title`, `heading` or `body`), `url` (what the app opens) and `web_url` (always a full link). Encrypted and password-protected items match by title only and never have a snippet. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for more. `ai_suggested` is `true` when `q` reads like a question. The first page of a search in a workspace (a `scope` or `current` you're a member of) is recorded without who ran it, for What people couldn't find; `log_id` names that record (else `null`).

paramNotes.scope: `all` (the default) or `workspace:<workspace id>` for one workspace.
paramNotes.updated: `week` or `month` keeps only what changed in that time.
paramNotes.current: The id of the workspace you're in: its items rank a little higher.
paramNotes.sid: A random id for this search box's session. A longer version of the last search in the same session updates its record instead of adding one. Never tied to you.

GET /api/v1/search/ai-status.title: Check AI search availability
GET /api/v1/search/ai-status.description: Whether Ask AI can answer now, for everything (no `scope`) or for one workspace. When it can't, `enabled` is `false`, `reason` says why (`off`, `not_configured`, `workspace_off`, `blocked`, `burst`, `user_daily`, `daily` or `monthly`) and `message` says it in words. `model` names the model it uses.

POST /api/v1/search/ask.title: Ask AI about your items
POST /api/v1/search/ask.description: Answers a question from the items you can open, with AI: AI turns the question into search terms, search finds up to 40 matching items, and AI picks the relevant ones and writes a short answer that cites them as [n]. Only text you can open is sent, never an encrypted item. Streams server-sent events: `status` (the stage), `results` (the matching items), `delta` (answer text as it's written), then `done` with `answer`, `citations` and `ranked`; or `limit` when an AI limit stops it, or `error`. Counts towards your AI limits.

GET /api/v1/ask/home.title: Get the home's Ask box
GET /api/v1/ask/home.description: What the home's Ask box shows: `status` (whether AI can answer now; when it can't, `reason` and `message` say why), `suggestions` (ready-made questions, each with its `intent`: `catch_up`, `my_actions` or `ask`) and `recent` (your latest conversations).

POST /api/v1/ask.title: Ask
POST /api/v1/ask.description: Answers a question from everything you can open (meetings and their transcripts, documents, pages, files and Guides) with AI, citing sources as [n] and meeting transcript moments as [n-sK]. Pass `thread_id` to ask a follow-up in a conversation, and `intent` `catch_up` (the last 7 days) or `my_actions` (your open tasks) for the ready-made questions; `question` may be empty with an intent. Pass `scope` to say what to answer from, as the in-app assistant does: `{"kind": "doc", "page": slug}` (that document or page first, then its workspace's meetings and documents), `{"kind": "meetings", "workspace": id}` (the workspace's meetings, optionally one `meeting`, a `series`, `since` and `until`), `{"kind": "folder", "workspace": id, "folder": id}`, `{"kind": "workspace", "workspace": id}` (Ask <Workspace>), `{"kind": "mine"}` (Ask my files: your own items outside any workspace) or `{"kind": "everything"}`; with `doc`, `context` (`heading`, `selection`) says where the reader is. One conversation (`thread_id`) can switch scopes. `page` alone (a slug) is the older way to ask a page. Every cited item is checked against your access again before it's returned. Streams server-sent events: `status` (the stage), `results` (the relevant items), `delta` (answer text as it's written), then `done` with `answer`, `citations` (each with `title`, `url`, `subtitle`, `quote` and, for a meeting line, `moment`), `ranked`, `thread_id` and `scope` (`kind`, `label`); or `limit` when an AI limit stops it, or `error`. Counts towards your AI limits.

example.question: When did we decide on Stripe Checkout?

GET /api/v1/ask/context.title: Get what Ask offers here
GET /api/v1/ask/context.description: The scopes the assistant offers for a place (`page`, `workspace`, `folder` and `meeting` query parameters): `scopes` (each `kind`, `label` and `sub`, only for things you can open), the `default` one, the `page`, `workspace`, `folder` and `meeting` they refer to, the workspace's meeting `series`, `workspaces` (every workspace you're in, for a chip each), `can_insert` (you can edit the page, so answers can be inserted into it) and `status` (whether AI can answer now, for meetings and for everything else). Something you can't open is left out, never an error.

GET /api/v1/ask/suggestions.title: Get suggested questions
GET /api/v1/ask/suggestions.description: What to ask right now. With `workspace` (an id): `team`, the workspace's live questions (each `topic`, `question` and `label`), written by AI from the last 7 days of meetings and pages that every member can open (never a restricted meeting or a private page) and the same for every member, with `updated_at`; `refreshing` is true while the first list is being written (ask again in a few seconds). And `personal`, your own (`label`, `question`, `intent`): your action items, your latest meeting. Without `workspace`, only `personal`. `ai_off` is true in a workspace with AI turned off. Reading the list never calls the model and doesn't count towards your limits. `404` when you aren't a member of the workspace.

GET /api/v1/ask/threads.title: List your Ask conversations
GET /api/v1/ask/threads.description: Your recent conversations, newest first: each one's `id`, `title` (its first question), number of questions and when it was last used. Only you can see your conversations.

GET /api/v1/ask/threads/{thread_id}.title: Open a conversation
GET /api/v1/ask/threads/{thread_id}.description: One of your conversations with every question and answer. Each answer's sources are checked against your access again: when you can no longer open one of them, that answer comes back with `withheld: true` and no text.

DELETE /api/v1/ask/threads.title: Delete all your conversations
DELETE /api/v1/ask/threads.description: Deletes every conversation you had with Ask. Your documents aren't touched.

POST /api/v1/search/click.title: Record an opened result
POST /api/v1/search/click.description: Marks the search `log_id` (from `GET /api/v1/search`) as having had a result opened, for What people couldn't find. Nothing else is recorded. Answers `204`.

GET /api/v1/search/quick.title: Quick search
GET /api/v1/search/quick.description: Finds files, folders and workspaces you can open by title, address or file name. Never searches content.

GET /api/v1/me/connections.title: List connected apps
GET /api/v1/me/connections.description: AI apps you connected to Markdrop through its approval screen.

DELETE /api/v1/me/connections/{client_id.title: Disconnect an app
DELETE /api/v1/me/connections/{client_id.description: Revokes an AI app's access at once.

POST /api/v1/meeting-memory/related.title: Related meeting facts
POST /api/v1/meeting-memory/related.description: Meeting memory for writing: the decisions, action items, open questions and topics recorded in a workspace's meetings that relate to what you're writing, best match first. Give `page` (a slug; its workspace is used and its own meeting left out) or `workspace`, and any of `title`, `heading`, `selection`, `section` or a free query `q`; `kinds` limits the kinds. Each fact has its `text`, `owner`, `due`, `status` (`open` or `done`, read from the meeting page), the `meeting` (id, title, date, series, link), `moment` (a link to the transcript moment, when you can open the transcript) and `markdown`, a dated, cited line ready to insert. `hints` are clear-match decisions the `section` seems to leave out. Only meetings you can open count; no AI call.

POST /api/v1/meeting-memory/check.title: Check a section against decisions
POST /api/v1/meeting-memory/check.description: Asks AI whether a page's section contradicts, leaves out or agrees with recorded decisions (`facts`: ids from Related meeting facts, at most a few). Returns a `verdict` (`contradicts`, `omits` or `consistent`) and a short `note` for each. For editors of the page. The same section and decisions are answered from a cache for 30 days (`cached`). Counts towards your AI limits; when a limit is reached or the workspace's AI features are off, `reason` and `message` say why instead of results.

GET /api/v1/meeting-memory/prefs.title: Get meeting memory settings
GET /api/v1/meeting-memory/prefs.description: Your own switches: `panel` (the From meetings button shows by itself) and `hints` (cards for missed decisions). Both are on by default.

PATCH /api/v1/meeting-memory/prefs.title: Change meeting memory settings
PATCH /api/v1/meeting-memory/prefs.description: Switches `panel` and/or `hints` on or off for you, everywhere. Returns both.

GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}.title: The Team board
GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}.description: Who is doing what in a workspace, for you: a card per member with `status` (`on_track`, `blocked`, `waiting`, `quiet`, or their own `self` / `away`), `now`, `targets` with `due` dates and `state` (`upcoming`, `due_soon`, `overdue`), `open_items`, 14 days of `activity`, and the source of their latest update; `blockers`, `projects`, `lanes` (projects × people) and `totals`. Every line comes from a meeting or page you can open now. Members of the workspace only. With Team memory off: `{enabled: false, can_enable}`.

GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/people/{.title: A person's Team page
GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/people/{.description: One member: `status`, `own_status`, `focus`, `working_on`, `targets`, `updates`, `action_items`, `decisions`, a `timeline` by day, 30 days of `activity`, recent `documents` and `meetings`. Each line has its `sources` (title, link, date, and a transcript `moment` when you can open it). On your own page, `hidden` lists the lines you hid or marked wrong.

GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/projects.title: A project's Team page
GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/projects.description: A recurring project (`key` from the board's `projects`): its latest `status`, `people`, `working_on`, `decisions`, `open_items` (action items, targets and blockers) and `updates`, each with its sources.

PUT /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/me/focus.title: Set your focus
PUT /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/me/focus.description: Your "What I'm focused on" note (up to 280 characters): it tops your card and your page for two weeks. An empty `text` clears it.

PUT /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/me/statu.title: Set your status
PUT /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/me/statu.description: Your own status (`text` up to 80 characters, an optional `emoji`, and `until`, when it clears): it replaces the status Team works out, for everyone, until then. An empty `text` and no `emoji` clears it. A status that says you're away (leave, holiday, out of office…) is never shown as quiet.

POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts/{.title: Hide a line about you
POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts/{.description: Hides a line about you from everyone, and keeps it hidden when its meeting or page is read again. Only the person it is about can.

DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts.title: Show a hidden line
DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts.description: Undoes Hide a line about you.

POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts/{.title: Mark an action item done
POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts/{.description: Marks one of your action items or targets done: it leaves your open items, the board and This week, and stays done when its meeting or page is read again. Only the person it is about can; 422 for other kinds of line.

DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts.title: Undo Mark done
DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts.description: Undoes Mark an action item done.

POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts/{.title: Correct a line about you
POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts/{.description: "This is wrong": `text` is what's right (shown instead, marked corrected); empty takes the line down. Kept when the source is read again, and given to the model so it isn't said again. Only the person it is about can.

example.text: Finished the Lever import, not Greenhouse

DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts.title: Remove a correction
DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/facts.description: Undoes Correct a line about you.

GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/groups.title: Team groups
GET /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/groups.description: The workspace's Team groups (`id`, `name`, `member_ids`). For admins also `suggestions`: a group per meeting series of the last 60 days, with the members at half or more of its meetings (only meetings you can open count).

POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/groups.title: Create a group
POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/groups.description: Admins: a new group with a `name` and `member_ids` (members of the workspace; anyone else is dropped). Names are unique in a workspace, ignoring case.

PUT /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/groups/{.title: Change a group
PUT /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/groups/{.description: Admins: rename a group or change its members (the whole list).

DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/group.title: Delete a group
DELETE /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/group.description: Admins: deletes a group. Nobody leaves the workspace.

POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/weekly/.title: Send the weekly summary now
POST /api/v1/team/{workspace_id}/weekly/.description: Admins: puts this week's summary together and sends it now (it goes out on its own on Mondays at 9 am, workspace time): emailed to the admins and owner, posted to the Slack meetings channel when Slack is connected, and kept as Team's This week card. Only lines from meetings and pages everyone in the workspace can open. Returns the `week` and what was delivered.

GET /api/v1/meetings/status.title: Meetings status
GET /api/v1/meetings/status.description: What the Meetings page of a workspace needs: whether meeting AI can run for you (`ai.enabled`, and `ai.reason` / `ai.message` when it can't), whether the Google Docs picker is set up and connected (`google`), the Meetings folder's id (`folder_id`, null before the first import), whether you can import (`can_import`: members and up) and the meeting `types`.

POST /api/v1/meetings/preview.title: Preview an import
POST /api/v1/meetings/preview.description: What an import would make, without writing anything: the meetings the sources become (notes and a transcript of the same call pair into one), each with its detected `title`, `date`, `duration_s`, `attendees`, number of transcript `segments` and whether Google's notes were found. Each source is `{name, text}` or `{name, data_b64}` (a .txt, .vtt, .srt, .sbv, .docx or .md file, base64).

POST /api/v1/meetings/import.title: Import a meeting
POST /api/v1/meetings/import.description: Turns transcripts and/or Google Meet's Gemini notes into meeting pages in the workspace's Meetings folder (made on the first import). Each source is `{name, text}`, `{name, data_b64}` (a file, base64) or `{google_file_id}` (a Google Doc picked in the Google Picker; needs Google Docs connected). `title`, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and `type` apply when the sources make one meeting; Each meeting is filed in Meetings › <series> when it's a recurring call (a name seen on two or more days), else in Meetings › Other meetings. `restricted: true` limits a meeting to its attendees who are members and `false` opens it to the team; left out, a 1:1 or two-person call is restricted and three or more people are the team. The AI summary is written in the background (`ai.state` is `pending`, then `done`); `wait: true` waits for it. Members and up. Returns `{meetings}`, each with a `status`: `imported` (new), or `duplicate` (a Google Doc already imported into this workspace: that meeting, unchanged).
