POST /api/v1/meetings/google/token.title: Google Picker token
POST /api/v1/meetings/google/token.description: A short-lived Google access token (scope drive.file) and the Picker's keys, so the browser can open the Google Picker on your own Drive. Markdrop can then read only the Docs you pick. 428 `reconnect_required` when Google Docs isn't connected.

GET /api/v1/meetings/connection.title: Google Meet connection
GET /api/v1/meetings/connection.description: Your Connect Google Meet connection (`connection`, null when you haven't connected), wherever it sends meetings, and, with `workspace`, the other members' connections into that workspace (`others`). Each has the `workspace_id` and `workspace_name`, `restricted`, `include_shared`, `connected_by`, `created_at`, `last_received_at`, `last_imported_at`, counts (`received`, `imported`, `attached`, `duplicates`, `ignored`), `last_error`, the script's last run as it reported it (`script`: `ran_at`, `mode`, `found`, `sent`, `results`, `skipped` by reason: `already_sent`, `too_old`, `not_yours`, `title`, `writing`, and `errors`), and `script_version`, `latest_script_version` and `needs_update` (the installed script is older than the one Markdrop hands out now). Never the token or the script.

POST /api/v1/meetings/connection.title: Connect Google Meet
POST /api/v1/meetings/connection.description: Makes your Google Apps Script for automatic import into `workspace` (members and up): a new token with the `meetings:import` scope, pinned to that workspace, shown once inside the `script` (Code.gs) with the endpoint filled in, plus the Apps Script `manifest` (appsscript.json) and the inbox `endpoint`. `restricted: true` restricts every meeting it imports to its attendees. `backfill_days` (0, 7, 30 or 90) makes the script's setup also bring in that many days of past meetings, oldest first and without notifying anyone. `tz` (the browser's IANA time zone) dates a Doc without a date in its title. `include_shared` (default true) makes the script also send the meetings shared with you (organized by someone else, so saved in their Drive). Connecting again replaces your earlier connection: its token stops working. 10 an hour.

DELETE /api/v1/meetings/connection.title: Disconnect Google Meet
DELETE /api/v1/meetings/connection.description: Revokes your connection's token at once: the script's next delivery gets 401 and it removes its own schedule. Meetings it imported stay. Returns `{disconnected}`.

PUT /api/v1/meetings/connection/check-no.title: Turn on Check now
PUT /api/v1/meetings/connection/check-no.description: Turns Check for new meetings on for your Google Meet connection: `url` is your script's Web app URL (Apps Script: Deploy › New deployment › Web app, Execute as: Me, Who has access: Anyone), `https://script.google.com/macros/s/…/exec` or a Google Workspace domain's `https://script.google.com/a/macros/<domain>/s/…/exec`; anything else is 422. `null` turns it off. The address is never returned, to you or anyone: the connection shows `check_now: {ready, last_at, last}`. 404 when you haven't connected Google Meet. Returns `{connection}`. 20 a minute.

POST /api/v1/meetings/check-now.title: Check for new meetings
POST /api/v1/meetings/check-now.description: The Google Meet scripts connected to `workspace` that have Check now on run now instead of at their next run (every 5 minutes): Markdrop calls each script's web app with a key only it and the script have, the script sends what's new to the inbox as usual, and this waits for them (up to about 50 seconds; a script still sending then answers `timeout`, and its meetings arrive as it sends them). Members and up; once a minute per workspace (429 `{error: "too_soon", retry_after, message}`). 409 `{error, message}` with `not_connected` or `not_set_up`. Returns `{ok, message, checked, failed, not_set_up, imported, attached, updated, not_ready, writing, remaining, connections}`; each connection: `{connected_by, mine, ok, error?, message?, found, sent, imported, attached, updated, not_ready, writing, remaining}`. `error` is `bad_key` or `no_key` (the deployment runs an older script, or setup hasn't run since the update), `too_soon`, `busy` (a scheduled run is going), `disconnected`, `failed`, `sign_in` (Who has access isn't Anyone), `not_script`, `unreachable` or `timeout`. 6 a minute per person.

POST /api/v1/meetings/import-link.title: Import meetings from Google Drive links
POST /api/v1/meetings/import-link.description: Up to 20 Google Docs or Drive links (`urls`: docs.google.com/document/d/…, drive.google.com/file/d/…, drive.google.com/open?id=…) into `workspace` (members and up), one result each in `results`: `{url, file_id, status, meeting?, meeting_id?, message?}`. `status`: `imported`, `attached` or `duplicate` (with the `meeting`), `queued` (the Doc isn't shared with "anyone with the link" and your Google Meet script is connected to this workspace: it fetches the Doc with your own Google access on its next run), `needs_access` (with what to do), or `error` (not a Google link). Markdrop fetches only Google's export of that file, following redirects only to Google's own hosts, with a timeout and a 4 MB cap. 1:1s and two-person calls are restricted to their attendees. 20 a minute.

GET /api/v1/meetings/import-link.title: Your Drive link requests
GET /api/v1/meetings/import-link.description: Your recent Drive link requests in `workspace` (newest first): `file_id`, `url`, `state` (`queued`, `sent` or `failed`), `error` (`not_found`, `unreadable`, `not_a_doc`), `requested_at`, `done_at` and `meeting_id`.

POST /api/v1/meetings/inbox.title: Meetings inbox (the Google Meet script)
POST /api/v1/meetings/inbox.description: Where the Connect Google Meet script sends one Google Doc: `{source: "google-meet-script", version, file_id, title, created, kind_hint, text, doc_url, owner, backfill, requested}`. `kind_hint` is `transcript`, `notes` or `unknown` (a Doc in a Meet Recordings folder: Markdrop decides). `owner` is the Doc's owner in Drive (`name`, `email`, `me`): who organized the call. `requested: true` marks a Doc someone asked for by pasting its link: it's imported like a manual import (notified unless the call is more than a day old). `backfill: true` marks a past meeting from the script's backfill: it's imported as history, and nobody is notified about it (its @mentions stay links). The meeting is dated by the date in Google's title, else by `created` in the connector's time zone. Authenticated with the script's `meetings:import` token (Bearer `mdk_…`), which works here and nowhere else and is pinned to one workspace; its owner must still be a member. Idempotent on `file_id`: returns `{status, meeting_id?, url?}` with `status` `imported` (a new meeting), `attached` (the other half of a call already in the workspace: notes for a transcript, or the other way round), `duplicate` (already here: the same Doc, a Doc imported by hand, or the same call by name, date and start time) `updated` (the same Doc sent again with new content: its meeting took the new notes or the longer transcript), `not_ready` (v4 and later: nothing in it yet, like Gemini's notes Doc while the call is on; send it again when Google changes it; to older scripts this is a 409 so they retry) or `ignored` (no transcript or notes in it 12 hours after Google made it). A meeting someone deleted isn't made again. 401 when disconnected, 403 when no longer a member, 409 while the same Doc is being imported, 413 over 1,500,000 characters, 422 for a malformed delivery. Rate limited per token: 30 a minute, 600 a day.

example.title: Weekly sync (2026-11-04 10:00 GMT+05:30) - Transcript
example.text:
Ada Lovelace: Let's ship on Friday.
Bo Chen: Agreed.

POST /api/v1/meetings/inbox/status.title: Meetings inbox: the script's run
POST /api/v1/meetings/inbox/status.description: The Connect Google Meet script (v2 and later) reports each run here, with its `meetings:import` token. `phase: "start"` returns `{ok, latest_version, queue, check_key}`: `queue` is the Docs someone asked for by link that this script should fetch first (`[{file_id}]`). `phase: "done"` stores how the run went: `version`, `mode` (`run`, `setup`, `backfill` or `check`), `include_shared`, `found`, `sent`, `results` (`imported`, `attached`, `duplicate`, `ignored`), `skipped` by reason (`already_sent`, `too_old`, `not_yours`, `title`, `writing`), up to 5 `errors` (`title`, `error`), and the queue's `queue_done` and `queue_failed` (`file_id`, `error`: `not_found`, `unreadable`, `not_a_doc`). v3 adds `remaining` (Docs left for the next run: a run sends for about 4½ minutes, at most 200), `shared_drives` (`on`, or `off` when the Drive API is off in the script's project) and `drive_project` (that project, up to 40 lowercase letters, digits and dashes); `GET /api/v1/meetings/connection` shows them as `remaining`, `shared_drives` and `drive_api_url`. v4 adds `results.updated`, `results.not_ready` and `skipped.not_ready` (Docs Google hasn't filled in yet), and `mode: "now"` (Check for new meetings); every answer carries `check_key`, the key Markdrop calls the script's web app with. Only counts: never the skipped Docs. The Meetings page shows it. 401 when disconnected. Rate limited per token: 30 a minute, 2,000 a day.

GET /api/v1/meetings.title: List meetings
GET /api/v1/meetings.description: The meetings of a workspace you can open, a page at a time, newest first. Each is a card: `title`, `date` (the day it happened) and `time`, `series`, `type`, the first five `attendees` and `attendee_count`, `slug` and `transcript_slug`, a line of the AI `summary`, the `decisions`, `action_items` and `open_questions` counts, `cover`, `restricted`, how it came in (`source`: `manual`, `auto` or `mcp`) and its AI summary's state (`ai`). Get one meeting for the rest. When `next_cursor` is set, pass it back as `cursor` with the same filters and sort for the next page. The first page also has `total` (how many match) and, for a workspace admin with no filter, `hidden`: meetings restricted from them, without a title, so they can delete them. Answers carry an `ETag`; send it as `If-None-Match` to get `304` when nothing changed.

paramNotes.q: Only meetings whose title, series or an attendee's name contains this.
paramNotes.sort: `date_desc` (default: meeting date, newest first), `date_asc` (oldest first; meetings without a date last either way), `title` (A to Z, any case) or `imported` (most recently imported first).
paramNotes.source: Only meetings that came in this way: `manual` (the website), `auto` (Connect Google Meet) or `mcp` (an AI app).
paramNotes.since: Only meetings on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
paramNotes.until: Only meetings on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD).
paramNotes.series: Only this series (any case), or `none` for meetings without one.

POST /api/v1/meetings/ask.title: Ask across meetings
POST /api/v1/meetings/ask.description: Asks a question about every meeting in a workspace you can open, as Server-Sent Events: `status`, `results` (the meetings used, best first, and the `scope`), `delta` (the answer as it's written), then `done` with the `answer` and its `citations` (`label`, `kind`: `segment` or `page`, `text` like "Ada Lovelace, 12:34", and `href`), or `limit` / `error`. `series`, `since` and `until` ask only those meetings; without them, a series or period named in the question is used ("in Daily Standups last month"), and `scope` says so (`detected: true`, with a `label`). Answers say when and in which meeting each point was made, and questions about the latest state prefer recent meetings. AI answers in English; each cited meeting is checked against your access again. Counts towards your AI limits.

example.question: What did we decide about pricing?

GET /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}.title: Get a meeting
GET /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}.description: One meeting you can open, with what you may do to it: `can_manage` (restrict to attendees: the page's owner), `can_delete` (the importer or a workspace admin) and `can_regenerate` (anyone who can edit the page). 404 when it doesn't exist or you can't open it.

PATCH /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}.title: Update a meeting
PATCH /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}.description: `restricted: true` makes the meeting page private with access for the attendees who are workspace members; `false` gives it back to the team and removes exactly those grants (the page's owner only). `type` changes the meeting's type (anyone who can edit the page). `series` puts the meeting in a series (or takes it out with `null` or ""); detection never changes it back.

DELETE /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}.title: Delete a meeting
DELETE /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}.description: The person who imported it, or a workspace admin or owner (any meeting, even one restricted from them): the meeting page and its transcript go to the Trash for 30 days and the stored transcript is deleted at once.

POST /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}/regen.title: Write the summary again
POST /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}/regen.description: Writes the meeting's AI sections again (summary, decisions, action items, open questions, topics) and waits for them. When nobody has edited the page since, it's rewritten; otherwise the new sections are added at the end. Anyone who can edit the page. Counts towards your AI limits.

POST /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}/ask.title: Ask a meeting
POST /api/v1/meetings/{meeting_id}/ask.description: Asks one meeting, as Server-Sent Events (`delta`, then `done` with the `answer` and its `citations`, or `limit` / `error`). The answer comes from the meeting's transcript (when you can open it) and its page, including edits, in English; citations open the transcript at that moment. `history` carries the last turns of the conversation (`{question, answer}`, up to 6). Counts towards your AI limits.

GET /api/v1/meetings/backfill.title: List your past-meeting imports
GET /api/v1/meetings/backfill.description: Your imports of past meetings into `workspace` that are open or finished and not dismissed, newest first. Looking at a running import also picks it up again after a server restart. An import is returned with its `state` (`draft`, `running`, `paused`, `waiting`, `done` or `cancelled`), `quiet`, `restricted`, `wait` (why and until when it waits: AI is paused for now under its fair-use limit), `counts` (`included`, `done`, `imported`, `attached`, `duplicate`, `failed`, `needs_date`…), `problems` (files that were skipped, and why), `estimate` (how many meetings are left to summarize, and whether AI can write them all today: `may_wait`) and `rows`: one per meeting found, with its `date` and where it came from (`date_from`: `title`, `created`, `content` or `user`), `title`, `series`, `kinds` (`notes`, `transcript`), `include`, `needs_date`, `dup` (`new`, `duplicate` or `attach`, with the meeting already here) and, once started, its `state`, `error` and `meeting_id`.

POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill.title: Start an import of past meetings
POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill.description: A draft import into `workspace` (members and up). Your open draft there is returned instead when you have one, so a review survives a reload. `quiet` (default `true`): nobody is notified about the meetings' action items; meetings older than a day are imported quietly either way. `restricted`: each meeting is restricted to its attendees.

GET /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}.title: Get a past-meeting import
GET /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}.description: One of your imports: the review before it starts, its progress after. An import is returned with its `state` (`draft`, `running`, `paused`, `waiting`, `done` or `cancelled`), `quiet`, `restricted`, `wait` (why and until when it waits: AI is paused for now under its fair-use limit), `counts` (`included`, `done`, `imported`, `attached`, `duplicate`, `failed`, `needs_date`…), `problems` (files that were skipped, and why), `estimate` (how many meetings are left to summarize, and whether AI can write them all today: `may_wait`) and `rows`: one per meeting found, with its `date` and where it came from (`date_from`: `title`, `created`, `content` or `user`), `title`, `series`, `kinds` (`notes`, `transcript`), `include`, `needs_date`, `dup` (`new`, `duplicate` or `attach`, with the meeting already here) and, once started, its `state`, `error` and `meeting_id`.

PATCH /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}.title: Change the review
PATCH /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}.description: Before the import starts: per row (`rows: [{id, title?, date?, series?, include?}]`) its name, date (YYYY-MM-DD, not in the future), series (`null` for none) and whether it's imported; and the `quiet` and `restricted` switches. A duplicate of a meeting already here can't be included.

DELETE /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id.title: Discard or stop an import
DELETE /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id.description: A draft or a finished import is deleted (`deleted: true`). A running, paused or waiting one is stopped (`stopped: true`): the meetings already imported stay, the rest are left out.

POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.title: Add meetings to the review
POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.description: Adds up to 25 sources at a time to a draft and returns the review: `{name, text}`, a file as `{name, data_b64}` (.txt, .vtt, .srt, .sbv, .docx, .md; 4 MB each), or a Google Doc picked in the Drive picker as `{google_file_id}` (read with your Google Docs connection; it's dated by the day Google created it when its name has no date, in your time zone: `tz_offset_min`, minutes east of UTC). Up to 300 sources per import. The same text twice, an empty file or one without a transcript or meeting notes is listed under `problems` instead.

DELETE /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id.title: Remove a meeting from the review
DELETE /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id.description: Takes a row, and its files, out of a draft.

POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.title: Run the import
POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.description: Starts importing the included rows in the background, oldest first, one at a time, each with its AI summary. Every included row needs a date (422 otherwise). It keeps going when the page is closed. When AI reaches its fair-use limit it waits (`state: waiting`) and carries on by itself when AI is available again.

POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.title: Pause an import
POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.description: Stops after the meeting being imported now; `resume` carries on.

POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.title: Resume an import
POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.description: Carries on with a paused import, or one waiting for AI (it waits again if AI is still paused).

POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.title: Retry a meeting
POST /api/v1/meetings/backfill/{job_id}/.description: Imports a meeting that failed again (its `error` said why). A finished import runs again for it.

GET /api/v1/meetings/series.title: List meeting series
GET /api/v1/meetings/series.description: The series of the meetings you can open in `workspace` (recurring meetings such as "Daily Standup"): `name`, how many meetings (`count`) and the latest one's date (`last`), most meetings first. Also `total`, how many meetings you can open, and `one_offs`, how many of them belong to no series.

GET /api/v1/meetings/organize.title: Preview Organize meetings
GET /api/v1/meetings/organize.description: Workspace admins and owners: what **Organize meetings** would do in `workspace` now, and its current or last run. `preview`: how many `meetings`, how many `series` folders they go into and how many go to Other meetings (`other`), how many would move (`to_move`) or join a series (`series_set`), the transcripts still listed beside their meeting page (`transcripts_to_hide`), and the biggest series (`series_names`: `name`, `count`). `job`: the run, as in **Organize meetings progress**, or null. Reading it also picks up a run a stopped server left behind.

POST /api/v1/meetings/organize.title: Organize meetings
POST /api/v1/meetings/organize.description: Workspace admins and owners: files every meeting in `workspace` the way new ones are filed. A recurring meeting (a name seen on two or more different days) goes to Meetings › <series> and gets that series, unless a person set its series; anything else goes to Meetings › Other meetings. Transcripts move with their meetings, series covers are set where nobody chose a cover, and empty extra series folders are removed. It runs in the background: the answer is `202` with the run (`job`) at once; follow it with **Organize meetings progress**. One run per workspace: starting it while it runs joins that run. Safe to run again. 12 a minute.

GET /api/v1/meetings/organize/{run}.title: Organize meetings progress
GET /api/v1/meetings/organize/{run}.description: A run of **Organize meetings** (`job`): `state` (`running`, `done` or `failed`, with a `message`), `done` of `total` meetings, how many moved (`filed`), joined a series (`series_set`) or got a cover (`covers`), how many couldn't be organized (`errors`, with a few `error_samples`: `title`, `error`), and once done the `folders` and `series` in use, `transcripts_hidden` and `duplicates_removed`. Poll it every second or two while it runs. The workspace's admins and owners; 404 for anyone else.

GET /api/v1/jira/status.title: Jira connection status
GET /api/v1/jira/status.description: What Workspace settings › Integrations › Jira shows: whether Jira is set up on this server (`configured`), the workspace's Jira site (`site`: name, link, default project and issue type, the projects on Team, who connected it, how many people connected their account), whether you can change it (`can_manage`: admins and owners), and your own Atlassian connection (`me`). Members of the workspace only.

POST /api/v1/jira/connect/start.title: Start connecting Jira
POST /api/v1/jira/connect/start.description: Returns Atlassian's consent address. `kind: "site"` (admins and owners, with `workspace_id`) connects the workspace's Jira site; `kind: "me"` connects your own Atlassian account (`back`: where to return on markdrop.in). Atlassian sends you back to markdrop.in, which finishes with **Finish connecting Jira**. 503 when Jira isn't set up on this server.

POST /api/v1/jira/connect/finish.title: Finish connecting Jira
POST /api/v1/jira/connect/finish.description: The end of Atlassian's consent: `code` and `state` from its redirect. Stores your Atlassian connection (tokens encrypted). The `state` is for the account that started, lasts 15 minutes and works once.

GET /api/v1/jira/sites.title: Jira sites my connection reaches
GET /api/v1/jira/sites.description: The Jira sites your Atlassian connection reaches, for an admin choosing the workspace's site.

GET /api/v1/jira/projects.title: Jira projects
GET /api/v1/jira/projects.description: The projects you can see on the workspace's Jira site (or `cloud_id`), through your own connection.

GET /api/v1/jira/issue-types.title: Issue types of a Jira project
GET /api/v1/jira/issue-types.description: The issue types you can create in `project`, through your own connection.

PUT /api/v1/jira/site.title: Connect the workspace's Jira site
PUT /api/v1/jira/site.description: Admins and owners: the Jira site (`cloud_id`, one your connection reaches), the projects on Team (`projects`; none: Team shows nothing from Jira), and the default project and issue type for new issues. Registers the webhooks that keep statuses in step.

DELETE /api/v1/jira/site.title: Disconnect the workspace's Jira site
DELETE /api/v1/jira/site.description: Admins and owners. Issues stay in Jira and links stay on pages; Team, status sync and chips stop until the site is connected again.

GET /api/v1/jira/me.title: My Atlassian connection
GET /api/v1/jira/me.description: Whether your Atlassian account is connected, as whom, the sites it reaches, and the workspaces whose Jira site it reaches. Never returns a token.

DELETE /api/v1/jira/me.title: Disconnect my Atlassian account
DELETE /api/v1/jira/me.description: Deletes your Atlassian tokens. Issues you created stay in Jira.

GET /api/v1/jira/page.title: Jira chips on a page
GET /api/v1/jira/page.description: The page's linked issues by block id, for you: key, status and assignee when your own Jira can open the issue, the key alone otherwise; and whether you can create issues from it (`can_create`, `can_edit`).

POST /api/v1/jira/draft.title: Draft a Jira issue from an item
POST /api/v1/jira/draft.description: The AI draft of an issue (summary, description, issue type, priority, assignee, due date, labels) from an item on a page (`slug` with `block`, `offset` or `selection`) or a Team line (`fact_id`), with the projects, issue types, priorities and people to pick from. Creates nothing. When AI can't run, the draft is the item as written (`ai: false`, `note` says why). Needs your own Atlassian connection (409 otherwise).

POST /api/v1/jira/draft/all.title: Draft Jira issues for a meeting's action items
POST /api/v1/jira/draft/all.description: Drafts for every open action item on the page that has no issue yet (at most 25), in one AI request. Creates nothing.

POST /api/v1/jira/issues.title: Create a Jira issue from an item
POST /api/v1/jira/issues.description: Creates the issue as you, with the reviewed `fields`, and links it to the item: the description gets the item quoted and a link back to the page or meeting moment. Returns the issue's key and link.

POST /api/v1/jira/issues/bulk.title: Create several Jira issues from a page
POST /api/v1/jira/issues/bulk.description: Creates an issue for each `items` entry (block id and reviewed fields) as you, and links each to its item. Each result says whether it was created.

POST /api/v1/jira/links.title: Link a Jira issue to an item
POST /api/v1/jira/links.description: Links an existing issue (`key`: a key or an issue link) to an item on a page. Your Atlassian account must be able to open the issue; needs edit access to the page.

DELETE /api/v1/jira/links/{link_id}.title: Unlink a Jira issue
DELETE /api/v1/jira/links/{link_id}.description: Removes the link (the issue stays in Jira). The person who linked it, or a workspace admin.

POST /api/v1/jira/links/{link_id}/retry.title: Sync a linked to-do to Jira again
POST /api/v1/jira/links/{link_id}/retry.description: Moves the issue to match the to-do (ticked: Done; unticked: To do), as you, after a failed sync.

POST /api/v1/jira/lookup.title: Live chips for pasted Jira links
POST /api/v1/jira/lookup.description: For Jira issue links pasted in pages: the issues your own Atlassian connection can open (key, summary, status, assignee). Links it can't open are left out.

GET /api/v1/jira/team/{workspace_id}.title: Jira on the Team board
GET /api/v1/jira/team/{workspace_id}.description: Each member's Jira issues in the projects on Team (updated in the last 30 days): with your connection, the issues your Jira can open (`mode: "details"`); without it, counts only (`mode: "counts"`). `no_projects` when an admin hasn't picked any. Cached for 5 minutes (`refresh=true` asks Jira now).

GET /api/v1/jira/team/{workspace_id}/peo.title: A person's Jira issues
GET /api/v1/jira/team/{workspace_id}/peo.description: One member's issues grouped as overdue, blocked, in progress, to do and done lately (details), or their counts (no connection).

GET /api/v1/slack/status.title: Slack connection status
GET /api/v1/slack/status.description: What Workspace settings › Integrations › Slack shows: whether Markdrop for Slack is set up on this server (`configured`), the Slack workspace connected here (`install`: its name, who connected it, the meetings channel, how many people linked their account), whether you can change it (`can_manage`: admins and owners), and your own link and direct-message preferences (`me`). Members of the workspace only.

POST /api/v1/slack/install.title: Start Add to Slack
POST /api/v1/slack/install.description: Returns the Slack address that installs the Markdrop app in a Slack workspace (OAuth). Slack sends you back to markdrop.in, which finishes with **Finish Add to Slack**. Admins and owners of the workspace. 503 when Markdrop for Slack isn't set up on this server.

POST /api/v1/slack/connect.title: Finish Add to Slack
POST /api/v1/slack/connect.description: The end of Add to Slack: `code` and `state` from Slack's redirect. Connects that Slack workspace to this Markdrop workspace (one Slack workspace per Markdrop workspace: 409 when it's connected elsewhere) and links your own Slack account. The `state` is for the account that started, and works once.

DELETE /api/v1/slack/install.title: Disconnect Slack
DELETE /api/v1/slack/install.description: Removes the Markdrop app from the connected Slack workspace and forgets everyone's Slack link here. Messages already posted stay in Slack. Admins and owners.

GET /api/v1/slack/channels.title: Slack channels for meeting posts
GET /api/v1/slack/channels.description: Channels the meeting notes can go to: public channels, and private ones the app was invited to (`/invite @Markdrop`). `shared` marks a channel shared with another organization (Slack Connect), where only meetings anyone with the link can open are posted. Admins and owners.

PATCH /api/v1/slack/settings.title: Choose the meetings channel
PATCH /api/v1/slack/settings.description: Sets the channel meeting notes are posted to (`meetings_channel_id`, one from **Slack channels for meeting posts**), stops posting (`clear_channel: true`), or turns automatic posting of new meetings on or off (`post_meetings`), or each person's action items as a direct message after meetings (`action_item_dms`, on by default). Admins and owners.

GET /api/v1/slack/action-items/preview.title: Preview the action-items messages
GET /api/v1/slack/action-items/preview.description: Admins and owners: from the newest meeting you can open that has action items with a person, who would get a direct message with their own items after it (`people`: name, whether they're a member, how many items, and how Markdrop would find them in Slack: `linked`, `email`, `name` or `none`), and what the fullest message would read (`message`: its items with due dates, `open_link` for a member, `organizer` to ask for everyone else). Nothing is sent and Slack isn't asked. `meeting` is null when no meeting has such items yet.

POST /api/v1/slack/link/start.title: Start linking my Slack account
POST /api/v1/slack/link/start.description: Returns the Sign in with Slack address that links your Slack account to your Markdrop account. Pass `workspace_id` (members of that workspace) or `team_id` (the Slack workspace a /markdrop link button names). Slack proves who you are there; Markdrop keeps no Slack token for you.

GET /api/v1/slack/link/info.title: The Slack workspace a link page is for
GET /api/v1/slack/link/info.description: The connected Slack workspace's name, and whether your account is linked in it already. 404 when Markdrop isn't connected to that Slack workspace.

POST /api/v1/slack/link/finish.title: Finish linking my Slack account
POST /api/v1/slack/link/finish.description: The end of Sign in with Slack: `code` and `state` from Slack's redirect. 409 when you signed in to another Slack workspace than the one connected.

DELETE /api/v1/slack/link.title: Unlink my Slack account
DELETE /api/v1/slack/link.description: Forgets the link between your Slack account and your Markdrop account in the Slack workspace connected here. /markdrop then asks you to link again, and Markdrop stops sending you direct messages there until it finds you again (turn Slack notifications on again, or link).

GET /api/v1/slack/me.title: My Slack notifications
GET /api/v1/slack/me.description: Whether your Slack notifications are on (`on`, off by default), which kinds (`prefs`), whether you get your action items after meetings (`action_items`, on by default and separate from `on`), and each Slack workspace connected to a Markdrop workspace you're in (`teams`: whether Markdrop found you there, as whom, and how: `email`, `oauth`, `install` or `legacy`). `configured` is false when this server has no Slack app.

PUT /api/v1/slack/me/notifications.title: Turn my Slack notifications on or off
PUT /api/v1/slack/me/notifications.description: `{"on": true}` turns on your own Slack notifications and looks you up by your Markdrop sign-in email in each connected Slack workspace; `results` says per workspace: `matched`, `linked` (already), `not_found`, `taken` (that Slack account is linked to another Markdrop account), `needs_update` (an admin must update the app's permissions), `token` or `error`, with a sentence to show. Nothing about any other email. 409 when none of your workspaces has Slack connected. `{"on": false}` turns them off; your Slack link stays.

PATCH /api/v1/slack/me/prefs.title: My Slack notifications per kind
PATCH /api/v1/slack/me/prefs.description: Which direct messages Markdrop sends you in Slack once your Slack notifications are on: `mention`, `signoff_requested`, `shared` and `access_request` (each on unless turned off). `action_items`: your own action items after each meeting (on by default, even while Slack notifications are off; turning it on also undoes a Stop these from your Slack account). Send only the ones you change. Bell and email notifications aren't affected.

POST /api/v1/slack/meetings/{meeting_id}.title: Post a meeting to Slack
POST /api/v1/slack/meetings/{meeting_id}.description: Posts the meeting's summary, decisions and action items (with Done buttons) to the workspace's meetings channel, again if it was posted before. Anyone who can edit the meeting's page. 409 with the reason when it can't be posted: no channel chosen, the app isn't in a private channel, or the meeting is restricted (only meetings everyone in the channel may open are posted).
